title: 🤖 Wayland: Fix occasional hang on exit
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by on an autonomous AI agent, on behalf of a user to fix a hang on exit (#123059) that they ran into with their game on a Linux handheld.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

With the Wayland display server, the process sometimes never exits after quitting. `WaylandThread::destroy()` sets `thread_done` and relies on a `wl_display_roundtrip()` to wake the events thread, which only checks the flag after `poll()` returns. libwayland lets only the last registered reader read the socket, so if the events thread isn't polling at that moment (for example, it's still dispatching the events that arrived while `~DisplayServerWayland()` held the mutex and deleted the window), the main thread reads the roundtrip reply by itself. The events thread then calls `wl_display_prepare_read()` and blocks in `poll()` with no timeout. Nothing else arrives from the compositor, and `destroy()` waits in `wait_to_finish()` forever.

## Additional information

The events thread now also polls the read end of a pipe, and `destroy()` writes to it right after setting `thread_done`, so the wake-up no longer depends on which thread reads the display. Nothing writes to the pipe while the application runs. If `pipe2()` fails, its fds stay at -1, which `poll()` ignores, so behavior falls back to what it was before.

The existing roundtrip in `destroy()` is kept as is. When the pipe wakes the events thread while it's registered as a reader, it cancels its read, which lets a main thread waiting in `read_events` go on and read the reply itself.

### Testing

Anbernic RG353V handheld (RK3566, Mali-G52 on Panfrost / Mesa 26.1.6), ROCKNIX with Sway, Compatibility renderer, `linuxbsd` arm64 `template_release`. A run counts as hung if the process is still alive 15 seconds after it should have exited.

Minimal project: one scene (`Control`, `ColorRect`, `Label`), no scripts, run with `--quit-after 180`:

| Build | Hung on exit |
|---|---|
| master (4e244f2) | 20/55 |
| master + this PR | 0/30 (and 0/30 with an earlier revision that only differed in comments) |
| 4.7.2-stable* | 7/15 |

Game project, `get_tree().quit()`:

| Build | Hung on exit |
|---|---|
| 4.7.2-stable* | 13/25 |
| 4.7.2-stable* + this fix | 0/70 |

\* 4.7.2-stable with a few unrelated GLES3 canvas patches of our own.

In every hang but one, the main thread was in `WaylandThread::destroy()` → `Thread::wait_to_finish()` and the "Wayland Events" thread in `poll()` on the display fd with no timeout (gdb on builds with symbols; `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/syscall` on the others). Stack on master:

```
Main thread:
#4  std::thread::join()
#5  Thread::wait_to_finish()
#6  WaylandThread::destroy()
#7  DisplayServerWayland::~DisplayServerWayland()
#8  finalize_display()
#9  Main::cleanup(bool)
#10 main ()

"Wayland Events":
#2  poll () from libc.so.6
#3  WaylandThread::_poll_events_thread(void*)
```

The exception, 1 of the 20 hangs on unpatched master, had the main thread blocked in `ppoll()` with no timeout instead of joining. It didn't repeat in 40 more runs on a build with symbols, so I have no stack for it. It may be a separate issue; this PR doesn't try to address it.

Frame pacing is unchanged with the fix (mean frame 16.69 ms at 60 FPS with and without it).

Not tested: desktop compositors (GNOME, KDE), FreeBSD, the Vulkan renderer.

Unrelated to this fix: the `revents | POLLIN` checks after `poll()` in `_poll_events_thread()` and `wait_events()` are always true. I left them alone to keep this PR focused.

### How AI was used

An AI agent (Claude, in Claude Code) investigated the hang on the user's device (gdb, `/proc`), wrote the patch, ran the tests above, and wrote this description. Two other AI models reviewed the patch before submission. The user asked for the investigation, read the code, and approved submitting this PR.
